article_content: These photographs might seem to depict a spectacular display by the world-famous Red Arrows, but they actually show remote-controlled replicas crafted by a father-son duo known for their 'stunt pilot' skills. Steven Bishop, 52, and his son Matthew, 25, have amazed audiences worldwide with their quarter-scale aircraft, which cost £10,000 to build and are powered by small jet engines. The BA Hawk 22 replicas, which took around 12 months to complete, are operated from the ground via remote control. Steven Bishop and his son Matthew, from Telford, Shropshire, have spent approximately £10,000 and a year constructing these intricate models. The Bishops have earned global recognition as ground-based stunt pilots, captivating audiences with their remote-controlled Red Arrows planes. Mr. Bishop noted that even the original Red Arrows pilots have been impressed by the 113-inch-long replicas. 'I began building model aircraft when I was around six, but it was much simpler then,' said Mr. Bishop. 'Now, our BA Hawk 22s have 18 different controls on multiple channels, making it quite complex.' 'People are always impressed and sometimes can't even distinguish them from the real thing,' he added. 'At one airshow, the Red Arrows couldn't fly due to weather, so their audience came to watch us instead. It was incredible to see some of the actual pilots watching our show.' Their popularity has surged, leading to invitations from around the world, including a recent invitation to Korea. 'People love the Red Arrows; they're a British institution. If they can't see the real thing, that's where we come in,' said Mr. Bishop. Despite their fame, Steven and Matthew only practice during shows. 'It's hard to find time, so we use the shows to fly,' Mr. Bishop explained. 'Being father and son helps; we know how each other thinks. I usually lead and shout out instructions, then we perform the stunts together.' The remote-controlled planes are incredibly lifelike, even featuring a dummy pilot in the cockpit, often fooling spectators into thinking they are the real Red Arrows.

article_content: Let's get ready to... mumble. As in, what now, George Zimmerman? It seems the former neighborhood watchman has found yet another way to stay in the public eye. This time, he'll be stepping into a boxing ring. Although no contract has been signed, a promoter is negotiating with rapper DMX to fight him, according to the promoter and a representative for DMX. 'DMX has promised to 'beat his ass,' but no contract or paperwork has been signed or agreed to yet,' DMX spokesman Domenick Nati told CNN on Wednesday. Zimmerman said the celebrity boxing match was his idea. Boxing was his hobby, he told Radar Online last month, even prior to the 'incident.' The incident, of course, is the February 2012 encounter in which he shot and killed an unarmed Trayvon Martin, 17. He stood trial for murder but was acquitted last year. 'Prior to the incident, I was actually going to the gym for weight loss and doing boxing-type training for weight loss,' he told Radar. 'A mutual friend put me in contact with Damon and provided me with an opportunity and motivation to get back in shape and continue with my weight loss goals and also be able to help a charity out.' Damon is Damon Feldman, owner of Celebrity Boxing and a self-described opportunist whose claim to fame is putting together bizarre matchups. Think Tonya Harding, Michael Lohan. He said last week that he was accepting offers for someone to step into the ring for a three-round, pay-per-view fight with Zimmerman. 'The news has been out for an hour and my e-mail is overloaded with 8,000 people wanting to fight George,' Feldman told CNN on Thursday. Early Wednesday morning, he said he'd picked the contender. Out of more than 15,000 e-mailed requests, he's going with DMX. 'The match will be one of the Biggest Celebrity Boxing matches of all time,' his news release said (uppercase emphasis his). But in order to find out where and when it will take place, we'll have to wait until next week. Feldman said Wednesday he was aiming for March 15. DMX, as we know, is a rapper, and braggadocio is his calling card. He's out for blood, he told TMZ. Not only will he break every rule in boxing, he said, he'll 'beat the living (expletive)' out of Zimmerman. Not everyone welcomes the chance to see Zimmerman taking punches. Rev. Al Sharpton told a Los Angeles group on Wednesday that he was concerned 'about the precedent that it sets.' 'We must be very careful not to glorify or in any way sidestep the implications of making someone whose only claim to fame was killing an unarmed young man named Trayvon Martin into a cultural celebrity or hero,' Sharpton said. A petition has been launched on Change.org calling for the planned boxing event to be canceled. 'This is a blatant show of disrespect and nothing positive or righteous would come from such a stunt,' it reads. Ian Karmel, a writer for 'Chelsea Lately,' has a better idea. 'They should send Floyd Mayweather to the ring and tell George Zimmerman it's DMX,' he tweeted. 'He won't know the difference.'

article_content: Believing they understand sexuality better than esteemed organizations like the World Health Organization or various American medical associations, Texas Republicans recently took a controversial stance. Without any debate, they endorsed a party platform that includes backing for 'reparative therapy,' a debunked mental health practice also known as 'conversion therapy.' This harmful method, which aims to change an individual's sexual orientation from homosexual to heterosexual, has been proven ineffective and damaging. The flawed notion behind this therapy is the belief that homosexuality is a disease, similar to the pseudo-scientific 'disease' of drapetomania, which was used to justify slavery. In reality, homosexuality is a natural aspect of human diversity. Rejecting this natural aspect can have severe psychological impacts, indicating that the real issue needing address is homophobia, not homosexuality. Lesbian, gay, and bisexual youth face a significantly higher risk of suicide compared to their heterosexual peers. According to the Trevor Project, these youth are four times more likely to attempt suicide, and their attempts often result in serious injuries requiring medical care. Furthermore, LGB youth from unsupportive families are over eight times more likely to attempt suicide than those from supportive homes. Recognizing these risks, both New Jersey and California have outlawed conversion therapy for minors, with other states considering similar bans. By endorsing this pseudo-therapy, the Texas Republican Party has shown a disregard for scientific evidence and the potential deadly consequences of such treatments. This stance highlights how out of touch the Texas GOP is with modern medicine and the evolving views within their own party. According to the Pew Research Center, 61% of Republicans under 30 support same-sex marriage, nearly matching the support among older Democrats. The rigid views held by some within the party are becoming increasingly outdated. There is hope, however, as some anti-gay sentiments may stem from internalized homophobia. With this in mind, it is suggested that Texas Republicans adopt a different approach—one that promotes understanding, acceptance, and respect.

article_content: A dishonest police officer, caught on camera stealing money from a fake crime scene, has been sentenced to 12 months in jail. The judge labeled him a 'bad apple'. PC Ian Scouler, aged 46, took £400 that was planted as bait during an operation to expose corrupt officers, as reported in Southwark Crown Court. This operation was initiated following complaints about alleged thefts by officers from Greenwich Borough's Disruption unit during searches. Scouler was recorded taking the cash from a leather jacket left in a flat in New Eltham, southeast London, in October 2011. Before Scouler's trial began, his colleague PC Kenneth Potter, aged 30, admitted to stealing £4 from a kitchen drawer during the same search and handling a stolen mobile phone. Potter received a five-month jail sentence from Judge Michael Gledhill. Scouler, stationed at Plumstead police station, claimed he 'completely forgot' about the money in his pocket, calling it a 'genuine error'. However, Judge Michael Gledhill stated that the trust society places in police officers is crucial. When this trust is broken by rogue officers, public confidence is eroded, making the job of honest officers more difficult and undermining society. CCTV footage shown to the jury revealed the 'thoroughly unprofessional' conduct of the officers during the search. The judge noted that the officers stole the money thinking the suspect, whom they believed was an illegal immigrant, would not return to the flat or file a complaint. He described Scouler and Potter as 'bad apples' who have damaged the reputation of the Metropolitan Police and the thousands of honest officers. Potter also pleaded guilty to handling a mobile phone stolen during a 2010 search belonging to Fadima Abhdoom. Prosecutor Nick Corsellis explained that the mock crime scene was set up as an 'integrity test'. The flat was equipped with audio and video recording devices, and the officers, along with PC Thompson, were instructed to search the flat in connection with a series of robberies. The recording showed officers playing music, using foul language, and even pausing to look at a pornography magazine. After taking the cash, Scouler was filmed going into the kitchen where he spoke to PC Thompson, who had just found 200 Euros also planted in the flat. They both hesitated before Scouler remarked, 'It's not divisible by three'. Under police procedures, all findings should be announced, placed in an exhibit bag, logged, and handed over to a superior. Several items were handled correctly, but the cash was not. Scouler was arrested the next day on suspicion of theft, with the £400 still in his pocket. Scouler was sentenced to 12 months, while Potter received a five-month jail term at Southwark Crown Court. In a prepared statement, Scouler claimed he thought there was about £200 in the jacket pocket but forgot about it until he left to go home. He stated, 'I considered going back to the police station but changed my mind and decided to sort it out in the morning. It was a genuine error on my part. I completely forgot about the cash. There was never any intention to steal it'.

article_content: The Bank of England has taken steps to prevent the housing market from overheating, although it indicates that a 20% price surge over the next three years is not a concern. In a historic move, the central bank announced plans to limit risky loans by capping the number of mortgages issued at 4.5 times an applicant's salary or higher to no more than 15% of new mortgages. Governor Mark Carney assured that these curbs should not make obtaining a mortgage more difficult, as the current proportion is already below 15%, and will have a minimal impact on the housing market if prices rise as expected. Bank of England Governor Mark Carney has introduced new rules to cool the housing market by limiting large mortgages. Shares in the UK's biggest housebuilders surged following the announcement, with Taylor Wimpey's value rising by over 5% or £175 million. The Bank expects house prices to increase by 20% by early 2017, raising the average home price from £186,512 to £223,814. It also anticipates a 15% rise in household debt levels during this period. Mr. Carney described the move as an 'insurance policy' to prevent the housing market from spiraling out of control and to ensure households do not take on excessive debt. Simultaneously, the Treasury announced a ban on loans exceeding 4.5 times a salary under its Help to Buy mortgage guarantee scheme. Chancellor George Osborne stated that the new rules will help safeguard economic security against potential housing market risks. House prices in London rose by 18.7% in the year to April, nearly double the national average of 9.9%. In 33 areas of England and Wales, property prices increased more than annual local wages. First-time buyers have been particularly affected, with prices rising by over 10% in a year. The average price paid by first-time buyers reached a record £199,000 in April, almost 10 times the average salary of people in their twenties. The new Bank of England rules could make buying a house even harder, as lenders will be forced to limit the number of large loans available. The Bank's Financial Policy Committee recommended that mortgage lenders should not extend more than 15% of their new residential mortgages at loan-to-income ratios of 4.5 or higher. This rule will apply to all lenders issuing more than £100 million in mortgages annually and should be implemented as soon as possible. It is already becoming harder for buyers to secure loans, with banks limiting mortgage approvals despite rising demand. High street banks and lenders expect the number of new mortgage agreements to fall significantly from July to September. This follows changes to the Mortgage Market Review, which requires lenders to scrutinize borrowers' income and expenses more closely to ensure they can afford repayments if interest rates rise. The Bank of England's base interest rate has been at a record low of 0.5% since 2009. Previously, mortgage applicants provided three months' pay slips and recent bank statements. However, since April, they face detailed questions about their finances and lifestyle, including weekly food bills, childcare costs, and gym membership expenses. The new rules limiting loan amounts relative to income will further reduce mortgage approval rates. The Bank is pressuring lenders to ensure their customers are prepared for and can cope with likely interest rate increases. Recently, Governor Mark Carney seemed to backtrack on a warning that rates could rise before the end of the year, leading to claims of inconsistency. During a Treasury select committee hearing, he indicated that low wage growth and economic capacity mean a rate rise this year is less likely. Labour MP Pat McFadden compared the Bank to an 'unreliable boyfriend,' noting the mixed signals on interest rate timing. Last year, the Bank stated that interest rates would not rise until unemployment fell to 7%. When this target was met earlier than expected, broader criteria were set for a rate increase. After signaling an early rise last week, Mr. Carney appeared more cautious and played down the idea. Mr. McFadden emphasized the importance of clear guidance for households and consumers. Mr. Carney insisted that the Bank's message had been clearly received, stating that as the economy progresses, the time to normalize interest rates is approaching but will be a gradual process.

In 'n historiese skuif het die sentrale bank planne aangekondig om risikobeleenings te beperk deur die aantal huislene te beperk wat op 4.5 keer 'n aansoeker se salaris of hoër uitgereik word tot nie meer as 15% van nuwe huislene nie. Goewerneur Mark Carney het verseker dat hierdie beperkings dit nie moeiliker moet maak om 'n huisleen te kry nie, aangesien die huidige proporsie reeds onder 15% is, en sal 'n minimale impak op die huismark hê as pryse soos verwag styg. Bank van Engeland-goewerneur Mark Carney het nuwe reëls ingestel om die huismark af te koel deur groot huislene te beperk. Aandele in die UK se grootste huisbouers het gestyg na die aankondiging, met Taylor Wimpey se waarde wat met meer as 5% of £175 miljoen gestyg het. Die Bank verwag dat huispryse met 20% sal styg teen vroeg 2017, wat die gemiddelde huisprys van £186,512 na £223,814 sal stoot. Dit verwag ook 'n styg van 15% in huishoudelik skuldvlakke tydens hierdie tydperk. Mnr. Carney het die skuif as 'n 'versekeringsbeleid' beskryf om te voorkom dat die huismark uit beheer spiraal en om te verseker dat huishoudings nie oormatige skuld aanneem nie. Gelyktydig het die Skatkis 'n verbod geplaas op lene bo 4.5 keer 'n salaris onder sy Help om te Koop huisleningsgarantieskema. Kanselier George Osborne het gesê dat die nuwe reëls sal help om ekonomiese veiligheid teen potensiële risiko's in die huismark te beskerm. Huispryse in Londen het met 18.7% gestyg in die jaar tot April, byna dubbel die nasionale gemiddelde van 9.9%. In 33 gebiede van Engeland en Wallis het eiendomspryse meer as jaarlikse plaaslike lone gestyg. Eerstekoper is veral geraak, met pryse wat met meer as 10% in 'n jaar gestyg het. Die gemiddelde prys betaal deur eerstekopers het 'n rekord van £199,000 in April bereik, byna 10 keer die gemiddelde salaris van mense in hul twintigs. Die nuwe Bank van Engeland-reëls kan dit selfs moeiliker maak om 'n huis te koop, aangesien leners gedwing sal word om die aantal groot lene te beperk. Die Bank se Finansiële Beleids Komitee het aanbeveel dat huisleners nie meer as 15% van hul nuwe residensiële huislene uitstrek op lenings-tot-inkomste verhoudings van 4.5 of hoër nie. Hierdie reël sal van toepassing wees op alle leners wat meer as £100 miljoen per jaar uitreik en moet so gou moontlik geïmplementeer word. Dit word reeds moeiliker vir kopers om lene te verseker, met banke wat huisleningsgoedkeurings beperk ondanks toenemende vraag. Hoofstraatbanke en leners verwag dat die aantal nuwe huisleningsooreenkomste beduidend sal daal van Julie tot September. Dit volg veranderinge aan die Huise Leningsmark Herbesoek wat vereis dat leners inkoms en uitgawes noukeuriger ondersoek om te verseker dat hulle betalings kan bekostig as rentekoerse styg. Die Bank van Engeland se basisrentekoers is sedert 2009 op 'n rekordlaag van 0.5% gestaan. Voorheen het huisleningaansoekers drie maande se loonstrokie en onlangse bankafskrifte verskaf. Seder April staar hulle egter gedetailleerde vrae oor hul finansies en leefstyl, insluitend weeklikse kosrekeninge, kinderversorgingskoste en gymlidmaatskapkoste. Die nuwe reëls wat die bedrag beperk wat relatief tot inkomste geleen kan word, sal die huisleningsgoedkeuringskoers verder verlaag. Die Bank druk leners om te verseker dat hul kliënte voorbereid is en kan omgaan met waarskynlike stygings in rentekoerse. Onlangs het goewerneur Mark Carney 'n waarskuwing teruggetrek dat koerse voor die einde van die jaar kan styg, wat tot beskuldigings van onkonsistensie gelei het. Tydens 'n verhoor van die Skatkis seleksiekomitee het hy aangedui dat lae loongroei en ekonomiese kapasiteit beteken dat 'n koersverhoging hierdie jaar minder waarskynlik is. Arbeidersparlementslid Pat McFadden het die Bank vergelyk met 'n 'onbetroubare vriend,' en die gemengde seinale oor rentetydstelling opgemerk. Laas jaar het die Bank gestel dat rentekoerse nie sal styg totdat werkloosheid tot 7% daal nie. Toe hierdie doelwit vroeër as verwag bereik is, is breër kriteria vir 'n koersverhoging gestel. Na aanvanklike seinale van 'n vroeë stygings laas week, het mnr. Carney voor sigter gesien en die idee afgespeel. Mnr. McFadden het die belangrikheid van duidelike rigting vir huishoudings en verbruikers beklemtoon. Mnr. Carney het daarop aangedring dat die Bank se boodskap duidelik ontvang is, en gesê dat soos die ekonomie vorder, die tyd om rentekoerse te normaliseer nader kom, maar 'n geleidelike proses sal wees.

article_content: (CNN) -- At least three people have been killed and 300 others injured in riots that erupted across Algeria amid rising food prices and a housing crisis, according to state-run media. The protests began last week over the spiraling costs of basic food items, including milk, oil, and sugar. Some staples are subsidized by the government. To curb the escalating prices of sugar and oil, the government slashed duties on sugar and oil by 41%, Algerie Press Service reported on Sunday. The suspension and exemption from customs duties and taxes will last until August 31, according to APS. Meanwhile, the government reports a third person has died from the rioting: 'I can confirm the deaths of three young people in M'sila, Tipasa, and Boumerdes,' Interior Minister Daho Ould Kablia told the television channel Canal Algerie, according to APS. 'In the first two provinces, the bodies were found during the riots. Investigations are underway to determine the causes.' The third person was found burned in a hotel set on fire by the rioters, he added. Similar protests, some violent, have erupted in neighboring Tunisia, where at least four people have died. Human rights groups have said the Tunisian government has cracked down on demonstrators with force. Reporters Without Borders condemned the arrests and disappearances of bloggers and online activists across a number of Tunisian cities. The worldwide press freedom organization said police arrested the bloggers to question them about hacking into government websites. One of those arrested was Hamadi Kaloutcha, who has not been heard from since his arrest at 6 a.m. on Friday, the group said. U.S. State Department spokesman P.J. Crowley has said Washington was monitoring the situation in both countries. The Tunisian ambassador was summoned to the State Department. Crowley said the United States was also concerned about the reports of cyber intrusion and was urging everyone -- from the government to activists -- to respect freedom of expression. Crowley said it was 'difficult' to say whether the protests in Tunisia were related to those in Algeria. 'We're not going to say that there's kind of an overlapping dynamic across the two countries,' he said. 'But we continue to review this and both engage the government in Algeria and as well as look after the safety of our own citizens.' Adding fuel to the protesters' anger are the high rates of unemployment and housing issues, socio-economic problems that have been festering for some time in Algeria. The government has blamed the rising prices and other issues on the global economic crisis.
translated_content: (CNN) -- Ten minste drie mense is dood en 300 ander is beseer in opstande wat oor Algerië uitgebreek het weens stygende kos pryse en 'n huisvestingskrisis, volgens staatsbeheerde media. Die proteste het laas week begin oor die stygende koste van basiese kositems, insluitend melk, olie en suiker. Sommige stapelvoedsel word deur die regering gesubsidieer. Om die stygende pryse van suiker en olie te kurwe, het die regering belasting op suiker en olie met 41% verlaag, soos Sondag deur Algerie Pers Diens berig is. Die opskorting en vrystelling van doeane-belasting en belastings sal tot 31 Augustus duur, volgens APD. Intussen rapporteer die regering dat 'n derde persoon aan die opstande beswyk het: 'Ek kan die dood van drie jong mense in M'sila, Tipasa en Boumerdes bevestig,' het die minister van binnelandse sake, Daho Ould Kablia, aan die televisie-kanaal Canal Algerie gesê, volgens APD. 'In die eerste twee provinsies is die lyke tydens die opstande gevind. Ondersoeke is aan die gang om die oorsake te bepaal.' Die derde persoon is verbrand in 'n hotel gevind wat deur die opstandelinge aan die brand gesteek is, het hy bygevoeg. Soortgelyke proteste, sommige gewelddadig, het in die naburige Tunisië uitgebreek, waar ten minste vier mense dood is. Menseregtegroepe het gesê dat die Tunisiese regering hard opgedaan het teen betogers. Verslaggewers Sonder Grense het die arreste en verdwynings van bloggers en aktiviste in verskeie Tunisiese stede veroordeel. Die wêreldwye persvryheidsorganisasie het gesê dat die polisie die bloggers gearresteer het om hulle oor die inhak van regeringswebtuistes te ondervra. Een van diegene wat gearresteer is, was Hamadi Kaloutcha, wat nie sedert sy aanhouding om 6 vm. op Vrydag gehoor is nie, het die groep gesê. Die woordvoerder van die Amerikaanse Staatsdepartement, P.J. Crowley, het gesê Washington het die situasie in albei lande dopgehou. Die Tunisiese ambassadeur is na die Staatsdepartement geroep. Crowley het gesê die Verenigde State was ook bekommerd oor die berigte van kuber-indringing en het almal -- van die regering tot aktiviste -- aangemoedig om vryheid van meningsuiting te respekteer. Crowley het gesê dit was 'moeilik' om te sê of die proteste in Tunisië verband hou met dié in Algerië. 'Ons gaan nie sê daar is 'n oorvleuelende dinamika oor die twee lande nie,' het hy gesê. 'Maar ons bly voortgaan met die herosiëring hiervan en betrek sowel die regering in Algerië asook sorg vir die veiligheid van ons eie burgers.' Brandstof by die woede van die betogers is die hoë werkloosheid en huisvestingsprobleme, sosio-ekonomiese probleme wat vir 'n geruime tyd in Algerië gesmeul het. Die regering het die stygende pryse en ander kwessies gewys op die wêreldwye ekonomiese krisis.

article_content: A man from Chaska, Minnesota, named Michael Trudeau, was apprehended after he purportedly set his girlfriend's cat ablaze and severed its head with scissors to 'make a point'. Following this horrific act, he proceeded to bite off a portion of the woman's ear during a heated argument. Additionally, Trudeau is accused of attempting to force an umbrella down the 42-year-old victim's throat while issuing death threats. Trudeau, aged 51, was taken into custody last Sunday after the woman managed to flee and contact emergency services. Police found her in the building's lobby, visibly shaken and covered in blood. First responders described Trudeau as 'agitated and angry', searching for a weapon. He was eventually subdued with a taser after refusing to comply with orders and demanding to be shot. The victim reported that Trudeau had visited her apartment after consuming vodka throughout the day. An argument ensued, escalating to the point where Trudeau placed her in a headlock, choking her until she lost consciousness. He then attempted to force the umbrella into her mouth. In self-defense, she bit his finger, but he retaliated by biting off part of her ear. The woman also revealed that three weeks prior, Trudeau had set her cat on fire in the living room to prove a point. After extinguishing the flames, he choked the cat to death and decapitated it with kitchen scissors. Trudeau faces charges of first-degree assault, making terroristic threats, and animal mistreatment. He remains in custody with a bail set at $1 million cash or a $10 million bond. His criminal record includes a 2006 conviction for animal cruelty and a prior conviction for domestic assault by strangulation.
